subject: Bank-issued attestation for TIN reconciliation — PO release pathway
message_1_subject: Bank-issued attestation for TIN reconciliation — PO release pathway
message_1_body:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for starting the onboarding packet. Our finance team flagged that the TIN on the W-9 you uploaded (Lum os Analytics, EIN ending in 324) doesn’t match the TIN we have associated with the ACH details you provided. To move the purchase order forward we need one of the following pieces of evidence: a) an IRS 147-C (TIN confirmation) or CP-575 letter, or b) a bank-issued letter on bank letterhead that explicitly states the legal account holder name and the taxpayer identification number (TIN/EIN). The bank letter should include a bank contact, date, and preferably account number or masked account digits for verification.

Can you check with your bank and upload the quickest available attestation? If you already have a signed W-9, please attach that as well so we can reconcile both items. PO creation is on hold until we clear this.

Goal: confirm acceptable evidence by EOD Monday so procurement can proceed with PO routing.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Procurement Operations | Redwood Inference
procurement@redwood.com

Attachment request: signed W-9 (PDF), bank letter (PDF).
message_2_subject: Re: Bank-issued attestation for TIN reconciliation — PO release pathway
message_2_body:
Hi Marcus,

Appreciate the heads up — I pulled the docs together and attached what we have. The bank provided a verification letter on their stationery that lists our legal name and the EIN; it is not notarized. I've also attached the signed W-9. If you need a notarized version or an IRS letter we can request one, but that may take longer.

I attached: lumos_bank_letter.pdf (bank verification), lumos_signed_w9.pdf (signed by our CFO).

Let me know if this is sufficient to unblock the PO.

Best,
Ben Harper

message_3_subject: Fwd: Bank letter from Lumos — need confirmation for TIN reconciliation
message_3_body:
Kimberly — forwarding Lumos' bank verification and signed W-9 below. The bank letter includes the EIN and legal name but is not notarized. Can finance confirm whether this satisfies our vendor TIN reconciliation criteria (i.e., bank letter with TIN + legal name + bank contact), or do we require IRS 147-C/CP-575/notarization? If acceptable, I will proceed to create PO and route for approvals.

Quoted message from Ben:
> The bank provided a verification letter on their stationery that lists our legal name and the EIN; it is not notarized. I've also attached the signed W-9.

Proposed next step if accepted: I create PO 4500542 in the system and send Lumos the payment remit form to confirm banking details before first payment.

Thanks,
Marcus
message_4_cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Harper <ben@lumos-analytics.com>
message_4_subject: Re: Fwd: Bank letter from Lumos — confirm acceptance and PO steps
message_4_body:
Marcus / team / Ben — the bank letter Lumos provided is acceptable for our TIN reconciliation provided it meets these checks: (1) legal name on the letter matches the legal name on the W-9 exactly, (2) the letter clearly states the EIN/TIN, (3) letter is on bank letterhead and includes a bank contact or verification reference. Notarization is preferred but not required in this case.

Action items:
- Marcus: create PO 4500542 and set payment terms as Net 30.
- Ben: please complete the payment remit form I attached below and confirm bank routing/account last 4 digits (for internal matching).
- Naomi/Jordan: flag any AP holds if the remit info differs from the bank letter.

Once we have the completed remit form + the bank letter + signed W-9 in the vendor file, finance will mark the vendor record verified and release the PO.

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf (vendor remit form included)
